chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim quoted Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Raqqi, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Jabalah, on the authority of Muawiyah ibn 'Ammar, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Abdullah, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), in a long hadith which he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

'No believer fasts the month of Ramadan seeking reward except that God, the Blessed and Exalted, obligates for him seven qualities: the first is that the unlawful (food) melts from his body; the second is that he draws near to the mercy of God, the Mighty and Majestic; the third is that it expiates the sin of his father Adam; the fourth is that God eases for him the pangs of death; the fifth is safety from hunger and thirst on the Day of Resurrection; the sixth is that God feeds him with the pure foods of Paradise; and the seventh is that God grants him immunity from the Fire.' He said: 'You spoke the truth, O Muhammad.'

key_terms.احْتِسَابًا: Seeking reward or divine pleasure through an act
key_terms.بَرَاءَةً مِنَ النَّارِ: Immunity or exemption from the Fire (Hell)
key_terms.سَكَرَاتِ الْمَوْتِ: The pangs or agonies of death
key_terms.طَيِّبَاتِ الْجَنَّةِ: The pure and good foods of Paradise

ai.seo_question: What are the seven rewards for fasting Ramadan according to this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* via the chain of al-Barqi, this hadith highlights the comprehensive spiritual purification of the fasting believer, linking physical abstinence to metaphysical rewards. It uniquely emphasizes the expiation of Adam’s sin and the ease of death (*sakarat al-mawt*), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the intercessory and purifying power of Ramadan devotion. The narration concludes with the Prophet’s affirmation, underscoring the authenticity and weight of these seven specific divine gifts.
